column1: # Why guidance is UP and synaptic function is DOWN in the same cells.
# Four tests, run on the rooted_v2 dorsal mapped object (11,554 cells).
1. Are the two panels' gene sets disjoint?
column2: 209 guidance genes vs 215 synaptic; 3 shared (Ank3, Cdk5r1, Met); Jaccard 0.007
column3: The opposition is not definitional - two near-disjoint gene populations move opposite ways

column2: guidance mean log2FC +0.048, synaptic -0.082, Mann-Whitney p=7.9e-3
column3: Opposite directions within one cell class

column1: 2. In WILD TYPE, do the two modules order along the trajectory?
column2: guidance rho +0.378; synaptic rho +0.544 (both p<1e-180, n=5,462 WT cells)
column3: Both rise with maturation, but synaptic rises FASTER

column1: 3. Does the guidance-minus-synaptic BALANCE shift with maturation in WT?
column2: rho -0.316, p=1.5e-126; declines monotonically from -0.007 (earliest decile) to -0.065 (latest)
column3: The balance is a genuine maturation coordinate: early cells are relatively guidance-weighted

column1: 4. Is the mutant balance shifted toward the early value?
column2: Cycling RG +0.0162 (p=1.5e-07); Immature astrocytes +0.0168 (p=6.7e-16); Deep-layer EN +0.0103 (p=8.3e-08); Upper-layer EN +0.0197 (p=2.7e-25)
column3: Mutant sits at a more guidance-weighted balance in every dorsal class

column1: 5. DOES IT SURVIVE MATCHING ON PSEUDOTIME?
column2: Balance difference shrinks across pseudotime quintiles: bin1 +0.0073 (p=0.003), bin2 +0.0089 (p=0.014), bin3 +0.0052 (p=0.10), bin4 +0.0019 (p=0.90), bin5 +0.0014 (p=0.59)
column3: 3 of 5 bins non-significant - most of the effect is explained by WHERE the cell sits

column2: pt coefficient -0.00630 (p<1e-300); genotype +0.00533 (p=6.0e-05); R2 pt alone 0.175, genotype alone 0.014, both 0.176
column3: Position carries the balance; genotype adds ~0.1% of variance on top

column1: residual genotype effect in pseudotime units
column2: 0.85 units, vs measured shifts of -1.54 (deep-layer EN) and -2.22 (upper-layer EN)
column3: Position accounts for roughly half to two-thirds of the balance shift

column1: # CONCLUSION: the opposite directions are consistent with mutant cells sitting
# earlier on the maturation trajectory, where the guidance-to-synaptic balance is
# naturally higher. That is a POSITION effect, largely reproduced by comparing WT
# cells at different pseudotime. A small residual genotype term survives matching
# (0.85 pseudotime units, R2 +0.001), so a position-independent component cannot be
# excluded, but it is not what the panels are showing.
